{{Quote|It's the droid, sir. It&hellip;it fell behind the group, and happened upon Gamma Squad's position. They&hellip;blasted it. Fortunately, the Princess and the others didn't hear the shots."''<br />''"Then ''you'' are the only fortunate one. Do not fail me again. Bring the droid here at once. Its memory might contain valuable information.|Lieutenant Sheckil and Darth Vader|<ref name="Thank the Maker">{{Tales|6|Thank the Maker}}</ref>}}
'''Sheckil''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Homeworld/Legends|hailing]] from the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]] and the [[Twin/Legends|twin]] brother of a [[Sheckil's twin|famous mercenary]]. A former [[Warrant Officer/Legends|warrant officer]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], Sheckil served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In early [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], in the wake of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], Sheckil accompanied the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] occupation force during the clandestine [[Occupation of Bespin|seizure]] of the [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] in a scheme to capture [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], and, ultimately, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. The Empire forced [[City/Legends|city]] [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] into accepting a deal in which the Empire would not permanently occupy Cloud City in return for Calrissian's compliance in helping to apprehend the Rebels.

The responsibility fell to Sheckil during the occupation to ensure Vader's command that the stormtrooper detachment remain out of sight until Vader himself was ready to seize the Rebels. However, the plan went awry when the Rebels' [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], unexpectedly happened upon the hidden position of an Imperial [[Gamma Squad (Imperial)|squad]], which then blasted the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] into bits. Sheckil retrieved the dismantled droid at Vader's order and presented its blasted pieces to the Dark Lord, who instantly recognized it as the same droid he had once constructed in his childhood. Although Vader ordered Sheckil to first have the droid destroyed, he later countermanded his decision by instructing the lieutenant to return C-3PO to the Rebels' [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] companion, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], thus paying respect to a lesson of responsibility he had learned while first building the droid. However, the mysterious moral was lost on Sheckil.

Following Vader's planned capture of the Rebels, Sheckil fell [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] himself upon attempting to escort the princess, the Wookiee, and the still-dismantled C-3PO to Vader's [[ST 321/Legends|ship]]. Calrissian defied his Imperial occupiers by organizing a team of his [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guards]] into a surprise ambush of Sheckil and four accompanying stormtroopers, placing them in Cloud City [[Cloud City Security Tower|captivity]] and helping his newfound Rebel companions to escape from Bespin.

==Biography==
===Managing the Cloud City occupation===
{{Quote|Shall I instruct the technicians to search its memory? Or&hellip;would you rather have the Ugnaughts smelt the thing? Sir?"''<br />''"The droid's parts carry the stench of Captain Solo's copilot. Deliver this box to the Wookiee's cell."''<br />''"I&hellip;forgive me, sir. I don't understand. You&hellip;want the prisoner to have the droid?"''<br />''"I am giving the Wookiee what he deserves."''<br />''"Oh. Yes&hellip;of course, Lord Vader."''<br />''"Captain Solo has an appointment in the interrogation chamber. Make sure he gets there.|Lieutenant Sheckil and Darth Vader|<ref name="Thank the Maker" />}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Sheckil was a native of [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]],<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Lieutenant Sheckil" /> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="Essential Atlas Online Companion">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> with a strong bond to [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture,<ref name="CSWE - Concord Dawn">{{CSWECite|I|137|Concord Dawn}}</ref> where he served as a [[Warrant Officer/Legends|warrant officer]].<ref name="Topps" /> Sheckil eventually earned a promotion due to his superb performance. He was also the [[Twin/Legends|twin]] brother of an [[Sheckil's twin|individual]] who became a famous [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]].<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Lieutenant Sheckil" /> By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], in early [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Topps" /> Sheckil served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]].<ref name="Rise and Fall">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

Shortly following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], he was part of the Imperial force, attached to the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] personal [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], that secretly [[Occupation of Bespin|occupied]] the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] in preparation of capturing the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] fugitives [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. Sheckil served directly under Vader's command during the occupation.<ref name="Rise and Fall" /> The Imperial occupation force arrived at Bespin well ahead of Solo and Organa's party, which also included the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] and the [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]. The Rebels had journeyed to Cloud City aboard the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] on a crippled [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] to seek refuge from Vader's forces with Solo's old friend, [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] of Cloud City. However, Vader had already coerced Calrissian into a deal in which Vader promised the Empire would leave the [[City/Legends|city]] unmolested once the Rebel quarry were captured, provided Calrissian cooperated with the Imperials. By the time the Rebels arrived, Sheckil and the occupation force were readied in position.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

[[File:Sheckil-ThanktheMaker.png|thumb|left|350px|Sheckil presents C-3PO's dismantled head to Darth Vader.]]
As the ''Millennium Falcon'' landed on Cloud City's [[Platform 327/Legends|Platform 327]], Sheckil waited out of sight within a Cloud City conference suite alongside Vader and [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] whom the Dark Lord hired to hunt down Solo and the Rebels. Sheckil, listening via [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] to an incoming progress report, kept Vader apprised of the developing situation, announcing as Calrissian led Solo and his unsuspecting group into the city. However, the situation soon turned complicated for Sheckil. No sooner had Vader reminded the lieutenant to keep his men out of sight and that the capture would ultimately be at Vader's command than Sheckil received a report that the Rebels' [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], C-3PO, had fallen behind the group and stumbled upon the Imperial [[Squad/Legends|unit]] [[Gamma Squad (Imperial)|Gamma Squad's]] position. The squad's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] promptly [[Blaster/Legends|blasted]] the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] into bits. Although Sheckil noted that, fortunately, the princess and the others did not hear the shots, Vader countered that Sheckil was the only fortunate one and ordered the lieutenant to bring the droid to him at once, for it might contain valuable information.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

Sheckil soon returned to the conference room with two stormtroopers, who carried an open container with the dismantled pieces of C-3PO inside. Holding up the droid's head for Vader's inspection, Sheckil noted that the droid's damage was, unfortunately, quite extensive and that the unit most likely belonged to the princess herself. He also pointed out that, judging from the way the droid had broken apart, it was most likely built a long time ago. As Vader looked closer at C-3PO, he quickly recognized it as the same droid he had once built as a young [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] boy living on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Watching curiously, Sheckil interrupted the Dark Lord's moment of nostalgia by inquiring whether he should have the Empire's [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] recover the droid's [[Memory bank/Legends|memory]], but Vader refused, declaring the droid useless and ordering Sheckil to have it destroyed.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

===Vader's trap===
Vader sprung his trap soon thereafter by capturing Solo and his group, planning to use them as bait for drawing his true target to Cloud City: his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Rise and Fall" /> While Vader revealed his presence to the Rebels inside of a Cloud City dining room, Sheckil stood by in an adjacent room alongside a waiting stormtrooper squad. He received a report via comlink of an alarming new development regarding C-3PO. Although his men had taken the droid down to one of Cloud City's smelting rooms to be destroyed, the droid had resurfaced during a search of the princess's quarters. Sheckil ordered two stormtroopers down to the junk room to question the [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] workers there just as Vader emerged from the dining room and ordered the waiting stormtrooper squad to escort the Rebel [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] to [[Prison/Legends|detention cells]].<ref name="Thank the Maker" /> With some excitement, Sheckil reported the news to Vader, who quickly started for the princess's suite to inspect the situation firsthand.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

[[File:Luke_Skywalker_TCGAR.png|thumb|right|220px|Luke Skywalker, Vader's target on Bespin]]
Sheckil followed quickly behind in Vader's wake through Cloud City's corridors toward the princess's quarters, where they found two stormtroopers standing with two Ugnaught workers&mdash;and the same container holding the dismembered C-3PO. Sheckil tried to rationalize his failure to destroy the droid by explaining to Vader that the Ugnaughts reported that the Rebels' Wookiee had broken into the junk room, retrieved the dismantled droid, and brought it straight to the princess. He also noted that, given the Rebels' apparent interest at preserving the droid, perhaps there was more value to the unit than realized.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

Once again, Sheckil asked Vader whether he should have their technicians recover the droid's memory or if he would rather have the Ugnaughts smelt it. After a moment of private contemplation, Vader rescinded his previous order and instructed Sheckil to return the droid to the Wookiee, much to Sheckil's bewilderment. When Sheckil inquired further, Vader explained only that he was giving the Wookiee what he deserved&mdash;a childhood sentiment of responsibility he had learned from his [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|mother]] upon first constructing C-3PO, the significance of which Sheckil did not grasp. With that, Vader departed, issuing one final order to Sheckil to see that Solo found his way to his scheduled appointment with Cloud City's interrogation chamber.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

===Calrissian turns the tables===
{{Quote|Hold them in the security tower. And keep it quiet. Move.|Lando Calrissian instructs Lobot following the ambush of Lieutenant Sheckil and the stormtrooper escort|<ref name="ESB" />}}
Per Vader's orders to Sheckil,<ref name="Rise and Fall" /> C-3PO was returned to the Wookiee, and the Empire thoroughly [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] Solo in the interrogation chamber, though Vader asked no questions of his prisoner. The Dark Lord merely used the Rebels' pain to send a signature through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] that would draw Luke Skywalker to Cloud City, presenting an opportunity for Vader to convert his son to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Later, Vader had Solo [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|encased]] in a block of [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] in one of Cloud City's [[Class three carbon-freezing chamber|carbon-freezing chambers]] as a test to determine whether Skywalker could survive the process himself. Skywalker arrived at Cloud City just as Solo's freezing concluded, and Vader ordered Calrissian to take Organa, the Wookiee, and the still-dismantled C-3PO to his [[ST 321/Legends|shuttle]] while he prepared himself to confront his son. Sheckil and a group of four stormtroopers escorted Calrissian and the Rebel prisoner processional through the city toward Vader's waiting [[Shuttle/Legends|ship]].<ref name="ESB" />

While Sheckil led the group through one of Cloud City's corridors, four blaster shots suddenly rang out from behind, catching the attention of Calrissian and Organa&mdash;unbeknownst to the group, Skywalker had entered the city and drawn fire from Boba Fett, who was himself leading Solo's carbonite slab through another corridor toward his own waiting [[Slave I/Legends|vessel]]. Calrissian took the opportunity to act. Adjusting his [[Cape/Legends|cape]] to shield his activity from Sheckil beside him, Calrissian tapped a key sequence into a small comlink on his wrist, transmitting<ref name="ESB junior novel">[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' junior novelization]]</ref> the command "[[Code Force Seven/Legends|Code Force Seven]]"<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> to his [[Aide/Legends|aide]], [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], Cloud City's [[Computer/Legends|computer]]-liaison [[Officer/Legends|officer]].<ref name="ESB junior novel" />

[[File:Sheckil-TESB30.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Using the Princess as a Human shield, Sheckil forcefully pulls Leia Organa through Cloud City's corridors.]]
Only a moment later, Skywalker rounded a nearby bend and encountered the prisoner procession. Sheckil was the first to notice a shadow moving along the wall of an adjacent hallway. The lieutenant stopped and gestured for Calrissian to open a nearby door for their escape. Moving quickly, Sheckil ordered the escorting stormtroopers to open fire on their pursuer and grabbed hold of Organa to drag her along,<ref name="ESB junior novel" /> using her body as a Human shield to protect himself.<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Human Shield">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=Human Shield}}</ref> Sheckil's stormtroopers fired several shots at Skywalker, forcing him to take shelter around a corner, while the group ushered the Rebel prisoners through the open doorway. Sheckil dragged the princess through last, but she momentarily grabbed hold of the door frame to scream a warning to Skywalker that he was walking into a trap. With one final tug, Sheckil finally pulled Organa through the door, and the group disappeared from Skywalker's sight.<ref name="ESB" />

The Jedi ran after them and stepped through the doorway, which remained open for him, but he entered only a dark antechamber with no sign of Sheckil or the Rebels<ref name="ESB junior novel" />&mdash;Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Bewil/Legends|Bewil]] had used his control of Cloud City's hatchways to restrict Skywalker's access, cutting off his pursuit<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Restricted Access">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=Restricted Access}}</ref> of Sheckil's group by lowering a [[Blast door/Legends|blast door]]<ref name="Star Wars 44">[[Star Wars (1977) 44|''Star Wars'' (1977) 44]]</ref> and thereby directing him toward the waiting Vader.<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Restricted Access" />

With Skywalker dispatched from their tail, Sheckil led his group down yet another of the city's corridors, completely unaware that he was about to be ambushed. As the group passed an intersection, Lobot and several of Calrissian's [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guards]] emerged from all sides, surrounding Sheckil and his stormtroopers with [[Relby-k23 blaster pistol|blaster pistols]] raised at the Imperials.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

Calrissian had turned the tables with his secret issuance of Code Force Seven, instructing Lobot to assemble a dozen of his personal guardsmen to rescue the Rebel prisoners.<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Sheckil and the stormtroopers were caught off-guard and unprepared, and they offered no resistance. The ambush a success, Calrissian shoved Sheckil toward one of his guards and confiscated each of the stormtroopers' [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]], then instructed Lobot to discreetly move the Imperials to Cloud City's [[Cloud City Security Tower|security tower]]. Lobot and the Cloud City guards then led Sheckil and the four stormtroopers away. Calrissian and the Rebels proceeded to safely escape from Bespin but at the expense of leaving Cloud City in the hands of the Empire.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|It was lucky the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} hyperdrive was damaged, or we wouldn't have reached the Bespin system before the Rebels!"''<br />''"Our journey to Bespin had ''nothing'' to do with ''luck'', Lieutenant Sheckil.|Lieutenant Sheckil and Darth Vader|<ref name="Thank the Maker" />}}
[[File:FashionableFelonFindsFormerFettFlatFooted-ESB.jpg|thumb|right|285px|Lando Calrissian's Wing Guards seize the unsuspecting Sheckil.]]
Lieutenant Sheckil, a former warrant officer on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of Concord Dawn, originally earned a promotion due to his stellar performance. During his service with the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]],<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Lieutenant Sheckil" /> he was trained to safely transport dangerous criminals and [[Politics/Legends|political]] [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]],<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and specialized in the transporting of high-profile criminals.<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Lieutenant Sheckil" /> Sheckil held a command role during the Empire's Bespin occupation, serving directly under [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader; however, his service on Cloud City was marred by constant failure.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

Although Vader instructed Sheckil to keep his men out of sight as Han Solo and the rest of the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} passengers arrived in the city, one of the occupation force's stormtrooper squads was unable to avoid having C-3PO inadvertently stumble upon its position, in which case the stormtroopers simply blasted the droid into pieces. Sheckil angrily derided his men as "imbeciles" for having done so. Later, Sheckil failed to have his men carry out the Dark Lord's order to destroy C-3PO's dismantled body;<ref name="Rise and Fall" /> and, finally, following Solo's carbon-freeze, Lando Calrissian and his guardsmen foiled Sheckil's efforts to escort the captive Princess Leia Organa and Chewbacca to Vader's waiting shuttle, after which Sheckil himself became a prisoner in the Imperial-controlled city.<ref name="ESB junior novel" />

Sheckil demonstrated a certain difference in perspective from the Dark Lord during the Cloud City occupation. Although the lieutenant credited luck for the Empire reaching Bespin ahead of the damaged ''Millennium Falcon'', thus allowing Vader time to weave his trap for the Rebels, Vader denounced Sheckil's analysis, declaring that luck had nothing to do with their journey. Later, after a reminiscent Vader recalled his [[Parent/Legends|mother's]] lesson of responsibility during his childhood and ordered the dismantled C-3PO be returned to the Wookiee, Sheckil was clearly confused and did not understand the Dark Lord's mysterious reversal.<ref name="Rise and Fall" />

Once Sheckil's group intercepted Luke Skywalker while escorting the Rebel prisoners through Cloud City to Vader's [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the lieutenant ordered his stormtroopers to open fire on the intruder<ref name="ESB junior novel" /> and immediately moved to take hold of the princess. He held her form in front of himself,<ref name="ESB" /> using her as a Human shield<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Human Shield" /> until he could move out of range of the immediate danger that Skywalker presented<ref name="ESB" />&mdash;a certain departure from the Imperial tenets of honor and bravery.<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Human Shield" /> Sheckil had [[Color/Legends|blond]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]], blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and light skin.<ref name="ESB" />

==Skills and abilities==
The Human lieutenant had an exceptional fighting ability, above average intelligence, average strength, speed, and diplomacy skills. He was not [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].<ref name="Galactic Files">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2|cardname=Lieutenant Sheckil (Imperial Officer)|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/93283/cid/6569532/2013-Topps-Star-Wars-Galactic-Files-Series-2-506-Lieutenant-Sheckil}}</ref>

==Equipment==
Lieutenant Sheckil wore the standard-issue [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]] during the Empire's occupation of Cloud City.<ref name="ESB" /><ref name="Thank the Maker" /> He frequently utilized a handheld comlink to manage the occupation force and keep Darth Vader apprised of developments.<ref name="Thank the Maker" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The actor to do that part wasn't available that day, so I filled in for him.|Jeremy Bulloch, explaining how he ended up playing Sheckil in ''The Empire Strikes Back''|<ref name="Star Wars Insider 30">{{InsiderCite|30|Head Hunter: An Interview with Jeremy Bulloch}}</ref>}}
[[File:JeremyBullochBobaFett.png|thumb|right|210px|Actor Jeremy Bulloch poses as the bounty hunter Boba Fett, his best-known role in the ''Star Wars'' saga.]]
Sheckil first appeared in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] as the unnamed [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] who escorts the captive Princess Leia, Chewbacca, and C-3PO through Cloud City to Darth Vader's ship before being captured himself by Lando Calrissian's security forces.<ref name="ESB" /> Prior to the film's [[May 21]] release,<ref name="Empire Turns 40">{{ThisWeek|6UccH037VQ0|The Empire Strikes Back Turns 40, Queen's Peril Gets a Voice, and More!|sw_url=video/the-empire-strikes-back-turns-40-queen-s-peril-gets-a-voice-and-more}}</ref> a film still of Sheckil was first included in''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'', a young-readers adaptation<ref name="ESB Storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> published on [[April 12]] in the same year.<ref name="Amazon-RandomHouse">{{Amazon|url=Empire-Strikes-Back-Storybook/dp/0394844149|text=The Empire Strikes Back Storybook}} {{C|US hardcover}}</ref> The character was portrayed by actor [[Jeremy Bulloch]], who is best known for also playing the masked [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter Boba Fett in both ''The Empire Strikes Back'' and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. According to Bulloch, the actor who was originally slated to play the Imperial officer was unavailable the day of shooting, so Bulloch filled in, thus providing fans a rare opportunity to see the actor outside of the Boba Fett costume.<ref name="Star Wars Insider 30" /> Sheckil was filmed between [[April 5]] and April 12 of [[1979]] on stage 2 of [[Elstree Studios]].<ref name="Making Of TESB">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

The Sheckil character was first identified by name and provided a brief backstory on the [http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/CloudCity-Dark/large/lieutenantsheckil.gif "Lieutenant Sheckil" card] from the [[November]] [[1997]] ''[[Cloud City Limited]]'' expansion set of the [[Decipher]] [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]. The card explains that Sheckil originated from the planet Concord Dawn and was the "twin brother of a famous mercenary," both intended as tongue-in-cheek references to Bulloch's dual portrayal of Boba Fett in the film.<ref name="Cloud City Limited - Lieutenant Sheckil" /> At the time of the card set's release, Boba Fett's character was [[canon]]ically established to have also originated from Concord Dawn, according to the [[1996]] short story ''[[The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett]]''.<ref name="The Last One Standing">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> However, the potential [[in-universe]] connection between the two characters was overridden with the release of the [[2002]] [[Prequel trilogy|prequel]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], which instead established Fett as a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] "[[Reproduction/Legends|born]]" on the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

Bulloch also portrayed the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Jeremoch Colton/Legends|Jeremoch Colton]] in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. In writing the [[August 31]], [[2004]] entry for the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[Episode III Set Diary]]," entitled [http://www.starwars.com/hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20040831.html "Inside the Alderaan Cruiser,"] author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] previewed the film's upcoming scene aboard the Alderaanian [[CR90 corvette/Legends|cruiser]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']],<ref name="Episode III Set Diary">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20040831.html|series=Episode III Set Diary|text=Inside the Alderaan Cruiser}}</ref> later established to be the [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']].<ref name="Star Wars Blueprints">''[[Star Wars Blueprints: Rebel Edition]]''</ref> Hidalgo revealed in the diary entry that Bulloch would be playing the ship's pilot, also noting that the actor previously portrayed Sheckil and jokingly considering the character's familial connections&mdash;"Makes you wonder if Sheckil has an Alderaanian relative."<ref name="Episode III Set Diary" />
